verification.title: Build verification: September 22, 2026
verification.summary: 22 of 22 automated checks pass locally and on Windows, Linux, macOS Intel and macOS Apple silicon runners. Each desktop archive was extracted and run on its own platform: two scenarios, video mode, GUI start. Both macOS archives were also run by hand. The web app ran a full scenario through the public site with report, CSV and summary downloads. Every PS row, shall item and deliverable re-read against 26169.pdf. The platform-maximum limit was re-measured at the allowed 10 deg/s and the faint beacon over ten seeds; both results are recorded as measured.
verification.note: Statuses are from runs in the repository, on GitHub Actions runners, and on the project server. Numbers quoted are measured, not estimated. Left for the team, not for the software: a hand-driven GUI session on a Windows and a Linux machine, a rehearsal of the 10 to 15 minute demo script, and, optionally, a narrated screen recording. Evaluator-supplied files arrive at the event; the template scenario and the video path are ready.

checks.name: Automated tests
checks.text: 22 of 22 pytest checks in about 15 s: geometry, gimbal limits, every path on screen and deterministic (seven kinds incl. user-defined waypoints), centroid accuracy, IMM prediction, closed loop clear, closed loop with vibration, identity under decoys, video path, PS rows 1 to 25 point by point. The same suite passes on the Windows, Linux, Intel Mac and Apple silicon runners.

checks.name: Scenario pack
checks.text: 13 scenarios (incl. the platform maximum at 10 deg/s), 15 s each, 3 seeds, compared run by run with the September 19 baseline: no run worse, four better. Clear line, circle and figure of 8: 6.4 to 8.2 px mean tracking error at 100% lock. Heavy noise 7.3 to 8.2 px, fog 6.6 to 7.3 px, low light 6.9 to 8.0 px, all 100%. Faint beacon 6.7 to 12.3 px at 91 to 97.5% over ten seeds (was not acquired at all). Multi-target stress 13.6 to 14.4 px at 98 to 99% on every seed (one seed was 69%). Acquisition 0.7 to 2.0 s everywhere except hard mode's 3 to 12 s sweep.

checks.name: Multi-seed envelope
checks.text: 3 seeds per scenario, all 13 scenarios; the faint scenario over 10 seeds. Clear, noise, fog, low light and faint pass every seed. The multi-target stress seed that swapped to a decoy now holds 98.8% lock at 14 px (candidates ranked by fitted width, which does not move with the noise level). Platform sway at the PS maximum holds 76 to 88% lock at 5 and at 10 deg/s alike: the random per-frame vibration is the physical limit.

checks.name: Truth independence
checks.text: The same random-motion run twice, the second time with ground truth deleted before the tracker: 0.000000 px difference in estimates and 0 px in the camera path over 240 frames. The tracker sees only the picture.

checks.name: Benchmark 2 path
checks.text: A synthetic 1200 x 1200 mp4 through the video input: 180 frames, lock 100%, CSV and PDF written. A 60 fps phone video tracked 669 of 754 frames with the 5 deg/s gimbal saturated 60% of the time.

checks.name: Standalone executable
checks.text: Four native archives from one workflow: Windows x64, Linux x64 (Ubuntu 22.04 glibc), macOS Intel, macOS Apple silicon. On each platform's own runner the archive was extracted fresh and the executable ran clear line, full stress and video mode, wrote report, CSV and summary, and the GUI stayed alive for 12 s: Windows 77/52/113 FPS, Linux 76/61/105 FPS, Intel Mac 76/41/87 FPS, Apple silicon 176/82/258 FPS, identical tracking numbers on all four. Both macOS archives repeated by hand on a Mac (Apple silicon native 238/108/367 FPS, Intel under Rosetta 2 174/115/236 FPS). The served archives are byte-identical to the tested ones.

checks.name: AI detector
checks.text: Kept as a gap-filling fallback (v2, 8 px validation localisation, 51% of measurements on a phone video). The faint-beacon case it was meant for is now handled classically by track-before-detect, so nothing in the specification depends on the network.

checks.name: Platform at PS maximum
checks.text: 20 px per frame sway plus 20 px per frame vibration: 76 to 88% lock over the seeds run, 25 to 27 px raw error, 23 px with the vibration removed. Measured again with the gimbal at the 10 deg/s the PS allows (platform_max_10degs.yaml): slew saturation drops from about a third of frames to 2%, lock and error do not improve. So the motor is not the limit; the random per-frame vibration is, and no controller can anticipate a random jump before the frame arrives. Every report under vibration now prints this in words beside the vibration-removed figure.

checks.name: Demo video
checks.text: About four minutes, composed by tools/make_demo_video.py from the engine's own frames: title cards, eight scenarios with scene view, camera view and live specification tiles, a Benchmark 2 segment on a video file, and a results card. On the site under downloads. A 10 to 15 minute live demo script is in docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md.

checks.name: Web app on the server
checks.text: Same engine served by FastAPI behind Caddy on a 4-core ARM server: clear line 123 FPS, full stress 59 FPS there. A noisy-line run through the public site in a real browser locked at 1.43 s, 68 FPS, 5 of 5 specification checks, report and CSV downloaded. One run at a time, any number of viewers, reconnect on socket drop.

checks.name: PS re-read
checks.text: 26169.pdf re-read on September 20: rows 1 to 25, the eight shall items, five deliverables, four evaluation stages. All mandatory items implemented and tested. Optional items: colour camera, multiple targets, spiral, sinusoidal and user-defined (waypoint) paths, all disturbance kinds. Only the optional demo video is not produced.

checks.name: Frame-rate independence
checks.text: The estimator-lag compensation was set in seconds but the filter delay is a number of frames, so at camera rates above 30 Hz (the PS makes the rate user-defined, 30 Hz minimum) the controller over-led the target. It now scales with the update rate. At 60 Hz the stress scenario went from 15% to 94% lock; at 30 Hz every scenario reproduces its previous numbers exactly. Confirmed on the full pack: 36 of 36 runs unchanged against the previous batch, none worse.

checks.name: Tracked rate metric
checks.text: Every report, results dialog, web finish panel and command-line summary now prints the tracked rate (share of frames in TRACK) beside lock retention (TRACK and centred within 30 px). High tracked with low lock tells a reader the camera could not keep up, not that the beacon was lost. No definition changed.

checks.name: Desktop interface pass
checks.text: Interface reviewed from screenshots at 1600 x 1000 and 1366 x 768. Fixed: camera view turning the sky white near the screen edge (contrast stretch counted the off-screen area), overlapping legend and cut-off HUD lines, plot legends over the data, meaningless idle axes, misaligned form columns, tiles keeping live values after a run instead of the report's numbers, spurious picture-shift readout, a stray scrollbar artefact, a font warning on start, the simulator button active with no video, and an empty-legend warning in video reports. Native system fonts and one widget style on every platform.

checks.name: Desktop and web are one interface
checks.text: Both front ends are generated from fsoc_tracker/ui_shared.py: the panel (all 52 fields in the same sections, labels, tooltips and ranges), the six tiles and their pass rules, the telemetry lines, the view captions, the end-of-run summary, help and welcome text, decoy generation and the camera contrast stretch. The web page has the desktop toolbar with Pause, Step, Save scenario, Screenshot, Results, Manual and About, all four plots and the same keys. Verified in Chrome: a full run with pause, one-frame step, resume and stop, a video run, and the return to the simulator. Remaining differences are the server's: views sent at about 15 fps, one run per server, files downloaded rather than opened.
